title: ForeSight-HF, a GPT-5 mini decision-support tool, scores two nursing-home heart-failure cases; patients managed independently
summary: Mount Sinai authors describe ForeSight-HF (GPT-5 mini on ProviderLoop) recommending diuresis for a warm/wet and de-escalation for a cold/dry nursing-home patient; both were managed independently.
account: Glajchen et al. (JACC: Case Reports, 3 June 2026) present ForeSight-HF, a clinical decision-support tool for heart-failure management in skilled nursing facilities that uses OpenAI's GPT-5 mini (accessed late 2025) on HIPAA-compliant infrastructure to synthesise unstructured documentation into heart-failure likelihood scores, exacerbation risk scores and management recommendations, reviewed by physicians in weekly interdisciplinary meetings on the ProviderLoop platform. Two cases illustrate it: a congested, well-perfused patient for whom it recommended intensified diuresis, and a hypovolaemic, hypoperfused patient for whom it recommended diuretic de-escalation. For each, the paper states that the patient remained at the facility for four months 'managed independently of the AI system'. The disclosures state that platform infrastructure was provided by ProviderLoop and that Dr Bander is its founder and owner; the earlier verifier set the case aside because outcomes are not attributable to the system. The date is the publication date.
purpose: Generate heart-failure risk scores and management recommendations from nursing-facility documentation
system: ForeSight-HF (large-language-model clinical decision support on the ProviderLoop platform)
developer: ProviderLoop (New York) with Mount Sinai clinicians
deployer: Skilled nursing facilities served through the ProviderLoop platform (location not stated)
segment: Heart-failure patients in skilled nursing facilities
taxonomy_note: Vendor-authored illustration (the senior author founded and owns the platform vendor); the two patients were managed independently of the system, so no outcome is attributable and the record is a general benefit with all depths null.

ratings.reason: Both patients were managed independently of the AI system; outcomes not attributable.
No measured organisational effect; prospective validation is called for by the authors.

ai_role.statement: The model generated recommendations that the authors judge appropriate in two contrasting cases, but the paper states the patients were managed independently of the system. The only source is the vendor-affiliated case report (senior author is the platform's founder and owner).
